A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CraftMesh and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references across 11 pages. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; no material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original quantitative comparisons, qualitative editing results, drag-based demonstrations, and component ablations in Section 4, Tables 1–2, and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: v3 reports original results on an expanded evaluation collection, including an additional competing method and mesh-generation-backend comparisons, alongside the retained editing demonstrations and ablations.

M1.justification: The image-editing, mesh-generation, Boolean/SDF fusion pipeline and its geometry and texture losses remain unchanged. Added alignment and texture-conditioning descriptions clarify implementation without establishing a changed procedure; the fusion block is also renamed.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 broadens the evaluation collection beyond v2's six illustrated sculpture/fantasy objects to assets selected from Objaverse-XL, Google Scanned Objects, and internet sources, including scanned household objects. The underlying mesh-editing tasks and drag-based demonstrations remain.

E2.justification: VoxHammer joins FocalDreamer, MagicClay, and Instant3dit in Table 1 and Figure 4. Trellis and Hunyuan3D 2.5 are alternative CraftMesh generation backends, rather than additional competing editing methods.

E3.justification: The stated evaluation expands from six objects to 100 models with three editing prompts per model. Section 4.5 also introduces alternative-generator configurations. The four evaluation metrics and reported GPU, iteration budgets, and optimization times remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 adds a backend sensitivity analysis comparing MeshyAI, Trellis, and Hunyuan3D 2.5. Existing geometry/texture component ablations and qualitative distribution-, gradient-, and boundary-loss removal tests remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates for the experimental results.

E6.justification: Both tables replace the retained methods' numerical scores and add results. CraftMesh's Table 1 scores change from 22.768/13.594/3.203/5.071 to 20.801/18.479/4.710/5.928 for CLIPsim/CLIPdir/NIQE/NIMA. These concern different evaluation collections, not same-setting performance changes. CraftMesh still leads the main comparison on all four metrics; VoxHammer and alternative-backend results are newly reported.

T1.justification: v3 adds an asymptotic complexity comparison asserting O(kn^2) for image-space Poisson processing versus O(n^3) for volumetric processing in Sections 1 and 3.2.1, without a derivation or proof. The existing mathematical definitions and equations remain, with texture-loss equations reordered.

C1.justification: The first contribution changes from introducing the 'first framework' to introducing 'a framework,' narrowing the novelty claim. v3 emphasizes SDF-domain Poisson fusion while retaining the central claims of high-fidelity editing, structural consistency, and versatility.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains that repetitive textures disrupt gradient-domain color propagation, motivating distribution alignment. It also interprets backend comparisons as attributing gains to fusion rather than a particular generator. The stated limitations concerning generative-model dependence and complex/open/noisy meshes remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page address, an alignment-method citation, and explicit edited-image conditioning for texture generation. It removes the post-acceptance implementation-release promise and the explicit description of supervision viewpoints as random. The PDFs do not establish actual code availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Google Scanned Objects, VoxHammer, and Imaginarium, and removes Deep Image Analogy. It refines positioning against classical Poisson mesh editing through connectivity and gradient-incompatibility arguments; most related-work coverage remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected introduction, related-work, and method paragraphs are rewritten. The fusion terminology changes, texture-loss explanations are reordered, and affiliations, contact information, and acknowledgments are revised. The overall section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 adds explicit texture-generation conditioning inputs, Figure 4 gains a VoxHammer column, and Tables 1–2 gain comparison rows. Front matter and surrounding text are reflowed, while the six-figure, two-table organization and retained demonstrations remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: v2's quantitative claims rested on six objects and one mesh-generation backend. v3's 100-model evaluation with three prompts per model, VoxHammer comparison, and alternative-backend analysis substantially strengthen the empirical foundation and address that narrow evaluation. Run-to-run uncertainty remains absent, and the new complexity and causal-attribution explanations are less firmly supported, but the overall evidential gain is substantial.
